title: Google Announces Agent Compute Engine for Secure AI Agent Execution
gist: Google announced Agent Compute Engine, a managed service running AI agents in isolated microVMs with checkpoint/restore and copy-on-write memory sharing, keeping all credentials outside the sandbox and injecting them through an external Agent Gateway. It is not yet available (preview targeted in coming months, no pricing, boot-time or density figures), and is Google Cloud-only, unlike the open-source Kubernetes-native Agent Substrate.

insights.claim: Google's Agent Compute Engine runs AI agents in isolated microVMs and keeps credentials, API keys and OAuth refresh tokens outside the sandbox, with an external Agent Gateway authenticating requests and injecting the required secrets.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Credential-free sandboxes are a differentiated security stance versus AWS and Azure agent runtimes — a selling point for regulated enterprises.
insights.locator: Google recently announced Agent Compute Engine

insights.claim: In Agent Compute Engine the orchestration harness (the brain) runs completely outside the execution sandbox (the hands), so untrusted guest environments only execute explicit commands dispatched by the harness, creating a deterministic audit trail linking each tool call to compute activity.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Brain/hands separation is emerging as the reference architecture for secure agent execution.
insights.quote: The orchestration harness (the brain) runs completely outside the execution sandbox (the hands)

insights.claim: Google designed Agent Compute Engine around three requirements: sandboxes free of exploitable credentials even when agents err, minimal cost and latency to resume idle agents, and persistent workspaces across sessions and OS updates.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: These three requirements define the competitive axes for agent infrastructure providers.
insights.locator: Google designed Agent Compute Engine to address three requirements

insights.claim: Agent Compute Engine uses copy-on-write memory sharing to run multiple agents on a single operating system template and pauses idle microVMs via fast checkpoint and restore.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Density and suspend/resume economics will determine the unit cost of hosting long-lived agents at scale.
insights.quote: using copy-on-write memory sharing to run multiple agents on a single operating system template

insights.claim: Agent Compute Engine targets four workload categories: interactive consumer and enterprise agents, persistent Linux workspaces for autonomous software engineering, large-scale parallel environments for model evaluation and reinforcement learning, and lightweight sandboxes for dynamic logic in Google services.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: RL and eval environments are a large compute-demand vector for sandbox infrastructure, not just end-user agents.
insights.locator: The architecture supports four main workload categories

insights.claim: Google uses the Agent Compute Engine platform internally for Gemini, Gemini for Business, the Antigravity agentic development platform, and model evaluation workloads.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Internal production use at Gemini scale lends credibility before external launch.

insights.claim: Agent Compute Engine is not yet available, has no announced pricing, and is targeted for preview in the coming months; Elementor's Harel Asaf notes the deep dive gives no boot time, price or density figure for it and the announced numbers belong to Agent Substrate.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Treat Google's agent-infrastructure claims as roadmap, not shipped capability, when comparing vendors.
insights.quote: The numbers in the announcement belong to Agent Substrate.

insights.claim: Google separately offers Agent Substrate, an open-source Kubernetes-native runtime that manages agent sandbox lifecycles independently of compute, suspending idle agents with state preserved and resuming them on available workers; it is portable across Kubernetes while Agent Compute Engine is Google Cloud-only.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Google is pairing an open portable runtime with a proprietary managed service — a classic open-core funnel into Google Cloud.

insights.claim: AWS and Azure offer comparable managed isolated agent execution through Bedrock AgentCore and Foundry Agent Service, but Google's approach differs by keeping credentials outside sandboxes and injecting them via an external gateway.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Agent runtimes are now a three-way hyperscaler battleground; security architecture is the differentiation.
insights.locator: Google is not the only provider

insights.claim: Google's agent governance stack includes Agent Gateway for traffic control and policy enforcement, Agent Registry for approved agents and tools, SPIFFE-based Agent Identity for authentication and auditing, and OpenTelemetry-compatible observability for model and tool calls.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Standards-based identity (SPIFFE) and telemetry (OpenTelemetry) signal agent governance converging on open standards.
insights.locator: Google also expanded its agent governance capabilities
